text:
Mia - Product: Quick sync — Acme wants a Q3 onramp for their feature that needs stable throughput + region isolation. They want production latency guarantees and audit logs. Can we scope what needs to happen across runtime/infra/security?
Jia - Eng Runtime: Thanks. Do we have target SLOs from them? p95 latency / throughput numbers?
Mia - Product: They asked for p95 <200ms for token gen at sustained 50 concurrent streams and 10k embeddings/day. Also must support VPC peering + audit export.
Omar - Infra: 50 concurrent streams + VPC peering is doable but we’ll need reserved capacity in the EU region. Timeline depends on capacity commits and infra changes (routing/firewalls). Estimate ~6w if we deprioritize other infra work.
Dylan - Security: VPC + audit export fine but we need KMS integration and an incoming compliance checklist. SOC2 evidence for key handling, and an initial threat model review. That will take ~2w gate.
Elaine - Eng: From product side, can we relax the latency target for MVP? Maybe p95 <300ms first, then tighten? That would reduce infra pressure.
Mia - Product: Acme says 300ms is acceptable for MVP if we commit to a roadmap to 200ms by GA. They care about predictable behavior and auditability more than absolute lowest latency day 0.
Jia - Eng Runtime: Ok — with 300ms we can prioritize quantized 8-bit weights + dynamic batching and prefix cache. Needs runtime work: kernel selection, burst autoscaling, and a canary for fallbacks. Rough engineer effort: 3w + 1w for canary infra hooks.
Omar - Infra: To support canary + reserved pool we need: (1) capacity reservation (2) routing policy for canary (region + fallback) (3) metrics export to Console. Each chunk is ~1w, parallelizable with runtime work.
Dylan - Security: I'll prep a minimal compliance checklist we can satisfy for an MVP private offering: KMS integration, retention policy, audit logs ingestion, and threat model notes. If we hit that, security can sign off on an exception for phased rollout.
Mia - Product: Good. Proposed split: Phase A (MVP hosted canary, p95<300ms, audit export, limited EU reserved pool). Phase B (dedicated capacity with SLA p95<200ms). Phase C (Private VPC + KMS). Acceptance criteria below.
redwood-bot: Deploy bot: new canary env created (env-id: canary-acme-eu).
Jia - Eng Runtime: Acceptance checklist (draft):
```
- Canary traffic routing live (traffic % toggle)
- Runtime quantization profile applied (docs + perf tests)
- Prefix/KV cache warmed for sample workloads
- Autoscaler policy validated at 50 concurrent streams
- Perf regression tests: baseline vs canary (p50/p95)
- Fallback to smaller model variant when capacity constrained
```
Omar - Infra: Infra checklist:
```
- Reserved instance/pool in EU provisioned
- VPC peering config + firewall rules (peer test passed)
- Logging pipeline -> Console (audit export) verified
- Metrics hook for per-tenant tracing enabled
```
Dylan - Security: Security checklist:
```
- KMS integration + key rotation docs
- Retention/ER logs retention policy agreed
- Threat model doc + triage notes
- Access review + least-privilege for service accounts
```
Elaine - Eng: Can we get owners? I can take the fallback model engineering + perf tests (2 engineers, 3w). Jia you own runtime quantization and canary hooks. Omar you own infra provisioning + routing. Dylan you own compliance checklist. Mia to own customer comms and acceptance sign-off.
Mia - Product: Assigning owners works. Target dates: Phase A demo to Acme in 5w, with weekly status. If blockers appear we push to 7w.
Jia - Eng Runtime: Noted. Quick question on fallbacks: do we fallback at request level or model-shard level? Prefer request-level to keep KV cache behavior predictable.
Omar - Infra: Request-level fallback is simpler for routing and tracking. We'll need a policy flag per request.
Dylan - Security: Make sure fallback logs include tenant id and reasoning for audit.
Mia - Product: ACTIONS: Mia -> confirm Acme cadence and accept phase split; Jia -> scope runtime tasks + list of perf test prompts; Omar -> reserve EU capacity estimate; Dylan -> initial KMS checklist by EOD Friday; Elaine -> perf harness and fallback implementation plan.
Elaine - Eng: I'll post the perf harness link in #eng-runtime tomorrow and tag owners.
Mia - Product: Thanks team. If no objections I'll lock the plan and send to Acme and growth this afternoon. :thumbsup:
Jia - Eng Runtime: No objections. Will start scoping today. :eyes:
Omar - Infra: Sounds good. I'll start a capacity request ticket and share ETA.
Dylan - Security: Will share checklist by EOD.
redwood-bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up in 1 week (thread: 1900012345). :bell:
